nodes.title: Give every slide a stable id
nodes.why: The dots render with @for and track slide.id, so each indicator keeps its DOM node when slides are added, removed or reordered.
nodes.alternative: Track the dots by $index, which ties each indicator to a position instead of a slide.
nodes.tradeoff: Every slide needs an id in its data, but the dots stay matched to their slides when the list changes.

nodes.title: Keep the position in one signal
nodes.why: The index is the only state that changes. The current slide, both edge flags, the helper text and the active dot all read currentIndex(), so one set or update moves all of them.
nodes.alternative: Keep a plain currentIndex field with getters, or store the current slide object next to the index.
nodes.tradeoff: Template reads need the call parentheses, but OnPush views see every change, including one made outside the template, such as by an autoplay timer.

nodes.title: Derive the current slide, or null
nodes.why: The ?? null fallback gives the template one value to test: @if (currentSlide(); as slide) renders the figure only for a real slide, and the computed recalculates only when currentIndex changes.
nodes.alternative: Read slides[currentIndex()] in every binding and render the figure unconditionally with non-null assertions.
nodes.tradeoff: The template needs an @if branch, but an index without a slide renders nothing instead of throwing on slide.imageUrl.

nodes.title: Derive the edge flags
nodes.why: The Next button binds [disabled] to !canGoNext() and next() checks canGoNext() as well, so the last-slide rule is written once; canGoPrev does the same for the first slide.
nodes.alternative: Compare the index with slides.length in the template and repeat the comparison inside next().
nodes.tradeoff: Two computed values for a three-slide list, but the edge rules sit next to the state they depend on.

nodes.title: Reject out-of-range navigation
nodes.why: goTo accepts any number, so it checks the range before currentIndex.set, which keeps currentSlide() pointing at a real slide for every caller.
nodes.alternative: Assign any requested index and rely on the dots only passing valid ones.
nodes.tradeoff: The guard is a small extra branch, but goTo stays safe if a keyboard handler or a test calls it with a bad index.
